a shift toward a smaller hemithorax indicates volume loss (hypoplasia/atelectasis), whereas a shift away suggests a space-occupying lesion (mass/effusion).", "Inspect the lung parenchyma for signs of hypoplasia, such as lobar aplasia, reduced vascular markings, or anomalous venous drainage (e.g., scimitar vein), rather than acute consolidation or large fluid collections.", "Differentiate between primary volume loss causing the shift versus secondary compensatory hyperinflation of the contralateral lung pushing the mediastinum; A) Improvement in COVID-19 pneumonia with resolving opacities.
B) Development of bacterial pneumonia with new dense opacities.
C) Progression of COVID-19 pneumonia with increased opacity density.
D) Onset of pneumothorax causing loss of lung volume.
E) Development of pulmonary thromboembolism resulting in peripheral opacities.
F) Onset of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) with diffuse opacities.
